Rails' Duration.build sets `variable` via `VARIABLE_PARTS.include?(part)` (activesupport/lib/active_support/duration.rb:206); trails' port derives it without the ported `include`/`includes` call. Unmasked by the RFC 0025 same-file-closure fix, not introduced by it.

Ruby `Hash#reject!` prunes the zero-valued entries of `@parts` in place; the TS constructor omits them while building the parts object, so there is no receiver to reject from. Surfaced by the DescendantsTracker `reject!` port making the name resolvable, not by a change in this file.

Rails builds the string via ISO8601Serializer#serialize; trails inlines it in iso8601 (the `new` half of the same call is already baselined above).

Rails' `Duration.parse` is `new(calculate_total_seconds(parts), parts)` (duration.rb:212-215) — the total is computed to fill the `value` constructor seat. trails' constructor is `(parts, variable)` and derives the total itself via `inSeconds()`, so there is no argument for the call to fill; `calculateTotalSeconds` is ported and holds the same PARTS_IN_SECONDS arithmetic.
duration.rb:155 is `new(value, { seconds: value }, false)`; the port drops the leading raw value and passes ({ seconds: n }, false) — Duration carries its value off the parts.
